GenerateAnimator.rationale: Presentation only (SHARED-FINDINGS section 4): no mechanical reader. The animator's Hit state is gated on IsAwake (SlumberingBeetle.cs:170), which is the flag's only reader besides its own setter - so IsAwake is presentation, and the sim's is_awake is likewise never read by a mechanic.

AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: The sim has no add-to-room phase - creature creation *is* construction - so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (slumbering_beetle.py:39-42). SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's shared verdict, copied: the game runs these from MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom via CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded (CombatManager.cs:860-867) inside StartCombatInternal (CombatManager.cs:394-398), i.e. after every creature is on the board and before Hook.BeforeCombatStart (CombatManager.cs:403); the sim runs them at create_monsters (combat.py:134), before relics attach (combat.py:157-159), before belt potions register (combat.py:164-166), before the parity Niche HP roll (combat.py:152-153) and before hooks.on_combat_start (combat.py:208). Same observable today on all three of section 2's clauses (listener set / HP-roll inversion / roll ordering); executed for this unit by `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b05.py rocket-ctor`, which prints the listener set at monster-construction time for a two-monster hive encounter: ['CombatHistory','StrikeCard','DefendCard', the previously-created monster's own powers] - no relic, no potion. Rule 7: the rationale leans on sts2_rl/combat.py, sts2_rl/relics/ruined_helmet.py, sts2_rl/relics/unsettling_lamp.py and src/Core/Combat/CombatManager.cs, which this record does NOT hash. Amounts and ORDER match: SlumberingBeetle.cs:76-77 applies PlatingPower PlatingAmount = GetValueIfAscension(ToughEnemies, 18, 15) -> 15, then SlumberPower 3m, both self-applied. The remainder of the override (:78-86) is the sleep sfx loop, the NSleepingVfx marker and a Died handler that only stops that vfx - all presentation.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: C# (SlumberingBeetle.cs:110-123): SNORE_MOVE.FollowUpState = ConditionalBranchState 'SNORE_NEXT', which adds (SNORE, HasPower<SlumberPower>) then (ROLL_OUT, !HasPower<SlumberPower>); ROLL_OUT.FollowUpState = ROLL_OUT (a self-loop); registered [SNORE, SNORE_NEXT, ROLL_OUT]; initialState = SNORE. slumbering_beetle.py:45-55 reproduces the graph, both branch predicates in the same order (keyed on 'slumber' in self.powers) and the same registration order and initial state. Because SNORE is a MoveState and it is the initial state, both machines start with a one-entry StateLog (seam step 28) and both take the sticky-initial-move early return on the first roll (seam step 30).

guards.what: WakeUpMove's body runs at damage time instead of on the beetle's stunned turn
guards.issue: In the game the damage wake DEFERS its effect. SlumberPower.cs:22-32's AfterDamageReceived decrements on unblocked damage and, at 0, calls CreatureCmd.Stun(Owner, slumberingBeetle.WakeUpMove, 'ROLL_OUT_MOVE') - and CreatureCmd.cs:875-890 / Creature.StunInternal make that delegate the PERFORM body of the synthetic MoveState('STUNNED', stunMove, StunIntent). So WakeUpMove - whose mechanical content is `if HasPower<PlatingPower> -> PowerCmd.Remove` (SlumberingBeetle.cs:104-107) - does not run until the beetle's own enemy-phase turn. The sim runs the whole of wake_up (slumbering_beetle.py:57-68) synchronously inside SlumberPower._count_down, i.e. during the player's turn, the instant the third unblocked hit lands. Executed with `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b05.py beetle-wake` on the ported SLUMBERING_BEETLE_NORMAL encounter: after hit 3, still on the player's turn, the beetle reads powers=[] (Plating gone), stunned=True, move=ROLL_OUT_MOVE - where the game would still show Plating 15 for the rest of that turn and through the enemy-turn-start decrement. LIVE by reachability (rooms.py:162 lists slumbering_beetle in the Hive normal pool; the probe drives the real encounter) - what is NOT proven is a damage-number consequence: PlatingPower grants block at BeforeSideTurnEndEarly (PlatingPower.cs:60-68) rather than reducing incoming hits, and both sides end the enemy turn with no Plating and no Plating block, so today the divergence is a power-list/state divergence inside the player's own turn (visible to a replay comparison and to the RL observation vector) rather than an HP swing. This entry deliberately does not touch the stun machinery itself - monster_state_machine G4/G5 own that, and the sim's stun (cmds.py:208-218) is not re-verdicted here. Rule 7: leans on sts2_rl/powers.py, sts2_rl/cmds.py, sts2_rl/rooms.py and src/Core/Models/Powers/PlatingPower.cs, of which only SlumberPower.cs and CreatureCmd.cs are hashed by this record.

guards.what: the natural (turn-count) wake needs no forced state
guards.rationale: SlumberPower.cs:41-52's AfterSideTurnEnd decrements and, at 0, awaits WakeUpMove directly - no stun, no ForceCurrentState. The machine then routes SNORE -> SNORE_NEXT -> ROLL_OUT on its own because the power is gone. The sim reaches the same end state by a different route: wake_up(stunned=False) calls machine.force_current_state(rollout) and sets _current_move (slumbering_beetle.py:64-66). Same next move either way, because SNORE_NEXT's !slumber arm is the only live branch once Slumber has expired.

Both halves of SlumberPower's countdown are modelled: unblocked damage decrements once per damage instance (SlumberPower.cs:24-26 -> powers.py:2158-2167) and the owner's own side-turn end decrements (:44-46 -> on_enemy_turn_end). Verified against the probe: three separate 30-damage hits against 15 block produce exactly one decrement each, and the first two leave Slumber standing. SlumberPower itself is the power tier's unit; only its beetle-facing contract is judged here.

RolloutDamage (DeadlyEnemies, 18, 16) -> 16 followed by StrengthPower 2m to itself (SlumberingBeetle.cs:43, 142-146); PlatingAmount (ToughEnemies, 18, 15) -> 15. Sim _ROLLOUT_DMG=16, _ROLLOUT_STR=2, _PLATING=15, _SLUMBER=3, with the damage before the buff.
SlumberingBeetle.cs:125-128 returns Task.CompletedTask; slumbering_beetle.py:70-71 is `pass`. The move exists only to carry SleepIntent and to occupy the turn.
SlumberingBeetleEncounter (slumbering_beetle.py:80-95) fields BowlbugRock, BowlbugSilk and the beetle in that order; the beetle is audited here and the two bowlbugs belong to another batch.
